artifact_handoff: The review created isolated admin-clean/npm-cache directories. A concurrent commit tracked them. Do not rewrite external history or delete tracked files blindly. After owner confirmation, add narrow ignore rules and untrack only these generated directories; retain business changes.
fingerprint_mismatch_policy: Re-read current source and user diff before applying a task; do not overwrite concurrent changes.

route_checker.limitations: Path-only regex check; request/response bodies and all clients are not covered.

bind_sql_model.scope: Exact schema/SQL in an in-memory SQLite model, not running Go handlers

android_xml.limitations: XML parse only; not APK compilation or device rendering.

shell_syntax.scope: fnOS build/lifecycle scripts, build/test scripts, android/gradlew; bash -n only

frontend_production_build.details: Fresh isolated npm ci --ignore-scripts succeeded; Vite failed because spawning esbuild was denied with EPERM. Existing dependencies also lacked Windows shims/native Rollup. No successful production build was obtained.

go_runtime_and_race.reason: Native Go absent from available commands; WSL returned access denied.

implementation_rules: Read git status/diff and every evidence location before editing; preserve all user changes.
Do not git reset --hard, git clean, delete databases/recordings, or run global pkill.
Prioritize P1. Respect dependencies and serialize overlapping write scopes.
Write a failing regression test, perform the smallest compatible fix, then run and record acceptance tests.
Do not disable unknown-field validation or add recover to hide the actual defect.
Keep private/LAN IPTV source support; authenticate and constrain proxy capabilities instead of banning every private IP.
Use isolated temporary databases, owned PIDs, dynamic ports, and controlled upstream fixtures.
Do not claim README tests, old APKs or old R8 output are new verification.
Do not change permissions to bypass sandbox denials; record unavailable toolchain/device checks.
Only mark a task completed after its acceptance criteria were executed successfully; otherwise keep pending verification.

tasks.title: Separate untrusted platform from administrator authorization
tasks.trigger: A client registers platform=admin and an administrator approves it as a normal playback device. Unapproved devices do not gain admin access.
tasks.impact: A playback device token becomes an administrator credential.
fix_steps: Whitelist platform values compatible with existing clients; never infer authorization from this display field.
Create server-owned roles/admin sessions and require reauthentication for untrusted historical admin records.
acceptance_tests: Approved normal devices cannot PUT system/config even if they supplied an admin-like platform.
Gateway administrator and password administrator still work; unauthenticated and pending devices remain denied.

tasks.title: Validate every config-loading path and generate persistent cryptographic secrets
tasks.trigger: Missing/mistyped config path, or an existing config with no secret. Normal fnOS installation with a generated random secret is a different path.
tasks.impact: Load can bypass validation and -check can falsely succeed; empty/PID-derived signing keys do not provide the claimed security.
fix_steps: Run normalization and validation before every successful return; explicitly supplied missing files fail.
Use crypto/rand for safe initialization, persist the secret with protected permissions, and reject empty/known placeholder values.
acceptance_tests: Missing config and placeholder secret produce explicit safe results; -check never falsely passes.
Valid initialization has a strong persistent secret across restart; empty-key forged stream signatures are rejected.

tasks.title: Synchronize fanout sends with subscriber closure
tasks.trigger: Disconnect/cancel/upstream replacement closes a subscriber between broadcast snapshot and channel send.
tasks.impact: send on closed channel in an upstream goroutine can terminate the service; HTTP Recoverer does not protect that goroutine.
fix_steps: Define a single close owner and a shared synchronization/state mechanism for send and close.
Remove the unsynchronized up.closed read; retain nonblocking delivery to slow subscribers.
acceptance_tests: Concurrent broadcast, cancel, replace and Close pass go test -race -count=50 without panic/race.
Slow subscribers do not block other subscribers; goroutines terminate after shutdown.

tasks.title: Bind HLS proxy target and operation scope into its signature
tasks.trigger: A holder of a valid playback signature changes the unsigned u parameter to a NAS-reachable HTTP/HTTPS target or reuses the signature on /seg.
tasks.impact: Channel playback authorization becomes an arbitrary HTTP proxy capability, including internal NAS services.
fix_steps: Sign canonical target URL, channel/stream, operation scope and expiry; only issue targets discovered in authorized playlists.
Constrain redirects/timeouts/resources and use administrator source policy without banning legitimate private IPTV networks.
acceptance_tests: Changing u, scope, channel, stream or expiry is rejected before upstream fetch.
Valid playlist/key/segment URLs and administrator-permitted cross-origin/private sources still work; a plain channel signature cannot proxy arbitrary URLs.

tasks.title: Align settings DTO, persistence and actual application semantics
tasks.trigger: The real settings form sends allow_lan, epg_refresh_hour, log_level and port in addition to accepted fields.
tasks.impact: Normal save returns 400; accepted changes are memory-only and can disappear or only change displayed values.
fix_steps: Use a single supported DTO; implement fields or remove unsupported controls, preserving unknown-field validation.
Persist validated settings atomically; apply supported runtime changes and clearly mark listener changes requiring restart.
acceptance_tests: Actual form payload succeeds and GET round-trip matches.
Restart retains values; effective listener/log state matches the UI or explicitly shows pending restart.

tasks.title: Make code redemption and rebinding a secure transactional state machine
tasks.trigger: Redeem generic code with device_id=0, redeem a code for an existing device using register, or rebind after local token removal with the same key.
tasks.impact: Code consumed but still pending, UNIQUE/409 before redemption, or lost local credentials that reapproval cannot restore.
fix_steps: Distinguish generic invitations and device-scoped codes; verify/associate/consume/approve/rotate in one transaction with one-use conditions.
Require ownership proof for bound-device credential rotation; never recover credentials from public device_key alone; surface invalid/expired code errors.
acceptance_tests: Generic code binds a new device once; scoped code binds only its target and failed matching does not consume it.
Two concurrent redeemers produce exactly one successful binding.
Android/iOS bind→local unbind→rebind succeeds; old credentials are revoked according to policy.

tasks.title: Make Swift wire DTOs compile and decode actual response shapes
tasks.trigger: Empty device config, direct response without expires, or EPG object decoded as array. Current worktree PlayerView also reads info.mode while the observed PlayInfo has no mode member.
tasks.impact: Potential current-worktree compile error and deterministic missing-key/shape decode failures before normal navigation or playback; no Swift compiler/device run was performed.
fix_steps: Recheck concurrent worktree changes, add required wire members and explicit decodeIfPresent defaults for optional response fields.
Decode the EPG envelope correctly and create fixtures from actual Go responses rather than assuming Swift property defaults apply to synthesized Decodable.
acceptance_tests: The latest iOS source compiles with all referenced PlayInfo members.
JSONDecoder handles empty config, missing optional expires/headers, direct/relay, disabled timeshift and actual EPG responses.
Newly approved iOS devices enter the homepage and can obtain playback info.

tasks.title: Allow VLC TS playback and request fresh HLS for AVPlayer fallback
tasks.trigger: VLC available, direct allowed, TS channel and correctly decoded play response.
tasks.impact: TS is rejected before VLC selection despite VLC supporting it.
fix_steps: Apply HLS-only restriction only to the AVPlayer path.
When VLC fails, request a new relay/HLS URL before AVPlayer fallback; never reuse bare TS for AVPlayer.
acceptance_tests: VLC + direct + TS produces video without the HLS-only error.
No-VLC build requests HLS; injected VLC failure makes a second relay/HLS play request and falls back successfully.

tasks.title: Preserve source headers through native direct and NAS relay/remux
tasks.trigger: Source requires UA/Referer/custom headers, or direct URL is inaccessible to a client but accessible to NAS.
tasks.impact: Direct clients discard headers; HLS/remux omit source-specific headers; changing decoder alone does not fix 403.
fix_steps: Decode/normalize/merge headers and propagate them through all supported engines and NAS playlist/segment/ffmpeg paths.
Auto mode retries through relay when necessary; forced-direct errors are explicit; never forward NAS authorization identity headers upstream.
acceptance_tests: Controlled UA=X and Referer=Y source verifies correct actual requests from TV, both phone playback entrypoints, iOS, relay and remux.
NAS-only reachable source succeeds via auto relay fallback; unsupported required engine headers do not silently disappear.

tasks.title: Keep true JNI callbacks and Gson remote targets in minified release
tasks.trigger: Minified release uses mpv/AVS3 or Gson remote-target model reflection.
tasks.impact: Reverse JNI callbacks/reflective fields are unprotected and an old R8 artifact lists removal. Current-device crash and current release output were not verified.
fix_steps: Keep real is.xyz.mpv.MPVLib class/callback names and signatures, not the obsolete bridge class.
Preserve or correctly annotate/move RemoteTarget reflection fields and constructors; do not globally disable shrinking.
acceptance_tests: Fresh release DEX retains event/all eventProperty overloads/logMessage and correct remote-target JSON fields.
ARMv7 and ARM64 minified releases execute mpv callbacks and remote target selection with correct IDs.

tasks.title: Embed the frontend built by the current release
tasks.trigger: Frontend source/dependencies change without a separate manual update of committed Go embed assets.
tasks.impact: Fresh frontend build may be copied to an unused package directory while the server serves old embedded assets. This does not assert current HEAD assets are definitely mismatched.
fix_steps: Choose one actual static-resource mechanism and build/synchronize it before compiling Go.
Remove dead external-copy/manual-dist dependencies and record frontend identity in package validation.
acceptance_tests: Clean checkout plus a unique frontend marker produces a server/fpk HTTP response containing that marker.
No manual committed dist synchronization is needed; served resource hash corresponds to the release build.

tasks.title: Resolve one version for all artifacts and never delete unrelated release tags
tasks.trigger: Push a v* tag differing from DEFAULT_VERSION or supply a new workflow version.
tasks.impact: Internal versions, artifact names and releases diverge; a new-tag run can delete the old default release/tag.
fix_steps: Resolve and validate version/ref/SHA once, then propagate it and compatible build numbers to all targets.
Remove blind release delete --cleanup-tag; implement controlled reruns while preserving original target commits.
acceptance_tests: v0.0.9 run has 0.0.9 in package metadata, filenames and release, all tied to the trigger SHA.
Existing v0.0.3 is unchanged; invalid versions fail before build; reruns cannot retarget/delete unrelated tags.

tasks.title: Carry selected stream into every signed relay request
tasks.trigger: Client selects stream_id while using relay rather than direct.
tasks.impact: Response reports the selected stream but actual handlers choose BestStream again; different requested lines collide in channel-keyed sharing.
fix_steps: Bind selected valid stream to signed playback context and validate channel membership.
Define safe sharing/replacement keys for TS Hub and remux instead of silently reverting to best stream.
acceptance_tests: Two distinguishable upstreams prove actual bytes from selected stream in relay TS/HLS/remux.
Cross-channel IDs are rejected; concurrent viewers' chosen lines are not silently replaced.

tasks.title: Recursively rewrite nested HLS playlists and URI attributes
tasks.trigger: Master playlist points to relative variant playlist containing relative segments/key/map.
tasks.impact: Child body is returned raw, so relative requests resolve against NAS /seg rather than the upstream playlist URL.
fix_steps: Reuse a bounded recursive playlist proxy using final response URL and target-bound signatures.
Cover segment lines and URI attributes, retain correct source headers, and control recursion/response size.
acceptance_tests: Master→variant→relative TS/AES key/EXT-X-MAP fixture plays through valid proxy targets.
Redirected playlist bases work; unsafe targets/oversize/deep recursion are rejected.

tasks.title: Separate device/admin session expiry from stream URL expiry
tasks.trigger: Configured token_hours elapses; device/admin credentials remain bound indefinitely unless revoked.
tasks.impact: Configured device/admin TTL is not enforced. Stream signature expiry is enforced and is not the same contract.
fix_steps: Define and migrate separate long-lived device credentials and short-lived administrator sessions.
Implement displayed TTL/secure renewal/revocation or remove misleading configuration; document active stream/WS revocation behavior.
acceptance_tests: Controllable-clock tests reject expired sessions while secure renewal works.
Revocation and existing stream/WS handling match documented policy without unnecessary valid-device rebinding.

tasks.title: Handle new remote play intents in singleTask PlayerActivity
tasks.trigger: TV PlayerActivity already exists and remote requests another channel.
tasks.impact: Server reports sent but the TV ignores the new channel because only onCreate reads its ID.
fix_steps: Implement onNewIntent/setIntent, validate against allChannels and invoke existing channel switch logic.
Add execution acknowledgement if the API promises executed rather than merely forwarded.
acceptance_tests: While playing A, remote B/C/A all update actual playback and OSD with one Activity instance.
Invalid IDs are safely rejected; a channel outside current group but in allChannels can be selected.

tasks.title: Make device config version and periodic heartbeat effective
tasks.trigger: Administrator changes config while a device continuously plays with no further API refresh.
tasks.impact: config_version uses unchanged bound_at and changes do not reliably apply; online state can age out despite ongoing playback.
fix_steps: Persist a monotonic version atomically with device configuration.
Use lifecycle-aware periodic heartbeats and validate/apply supported configuration on version changes; unsupported controls are not reported as applied.
acceptance_tests: During continuous playback, a config change applies within one documented interval; unchanged config does not rebuild players repeatedly.
Long playback remains online; background/exit stops timers and error/revocation handling is explicit.

tasks.title: Safely encode wizard credentials before replacing YAML config
tasks.trigger: Password contains quote/backslash or another YAML-sensitive sequence.
tasks.impact: Plain interpolation changes parsed credentials or breaks config and restart; avoiding sed/awk expansion is not YAML escaping.
fix_steps: Use a YAML encoder/safe scalar serialization, protected permissions and atomic replacement.
Validate new config before restarting and retain old config on failure; never log the password.
acceptance_tests: Quote/backslash/&/$/Unicode fixtures parse exactly to their original passwords in install and config update.
Invalid generated config does not replace working config or stop the existing service; permissions meet secret-storage policy.

Abort/generation protection against out-of-order frontend play/list responses
PR/push contract/race/release/package gates; nonzero checker failures and owned-PID shell tests
Official distribution trust/checksum and compatible signing migration; no credential disclosure claim
